answer: Recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments fortify Sybil resistance by binding identities to provable historical behavior, creating an immutable ledge of trust. Verifiable delay primitives, such as cryptographic time-stamping, overlay this ledge with a layer of temporal velvet, ensuring gradual reputation accumulation. Such mechanisms transform identity cloning into an exponentially hard problem, as adversaries must simulate provable elapsed activity across a garden of independently verifiable events.
